text:
maya: Heads up — seeing a customer escalation (ticket #2321) about a big tail increase on generation API from ~08:10 UTC. p95 jumped ~2x, p99 ~3x for a handful of routes in us-west-2. Support forwarded traces. Anyone oncall? :eyes:

liam: On it. Which dashboards are showing the delta? I see a small uptick in overall error rate but not huge.

maya: Two dashboards: 'prod / inference / latency' (panel A) shows p99 spike starting 08:09; 'traffic / route' panel (panel B) looks flatter. Support attached trace ids: trace-7f3a and trace-7f3b.

devon: panel A uses this prom query: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))` — panel B is an aggregate timeseries using `quantile_over_time(0.99, request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])` in the viz backend. Aggregation semantics differ. Could be a rollup vs raw-bucket mismatch.

maya: Ah — that would explain some disagreements. But the customer sees real-time slowness in traces (span durations corroborate). So there is a real regression, not just a dashboard bug.

ashley: Checking infra: noticed a canary rollout of inference-runtime v2.14 at 08:05 in us-west-2. 2 nodes got the new image, autoscaler bumped a few pods. CPU spiked around 08:07-08:12. Logs show a few OOM-kill attempts on the canary pods around 08:09.

liam: Can we get the deployment history?

ashley: Paste of commands I ran:```sh
kubectl -n prod rollout history deployment/inference-runtime
# revision 12 -> v2.13
# revision 13 -> v2.14 (canary)
kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=inference-runtime -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, image: .spec.containers[0].image, cpu: .status.containerStatuses[0].lastState}'
```

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026. Priority P2. Linked ticket #2321. Pinged runtime team.

devon: Repro steps for support to collect traces from customer (if needed):
1) Curl the route with the same payload and header that customer used
```sh
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: repro-<random>" \
  -d '{"model": "redwood-open-13b", "prompt": "<customer-prompt>", "max_tokens": 256}'
```
2) Share `X-Request-ID` value so we can lookup trace in jaeger and logs

liam: Quick metric checks: running top of query windows — p95 from raw histogram shows spike, but when I compute quantile from rollup metric over 1h the spike is smoothed. That matches the two dashboards disagreement. Still, traces show many long spans so there is a real tail increase.

maya: Any recent runtime config changes besides the canary? Batching parameters? Cache TTL?

ashley: Ops changed default `max_batch_size` for the new image to 64 (old was 32) and `batch_timeout_ms` was bumped to 40ms to improve throughput. That can increase tail latency for small concurrent workloads. Also some pinning changes in kernel selection for newer gpu drivers.

devon: That combination explains it: larger batches + slight timeout increase -> some requests waiting longer for batch formation; with a canary proportion it inflates p95/p99. Also if the canary had occasional kernel stalls (driver mismatch) you'd see OOM/log retries -> longer tails.

liam: Mitigation plan (short-term):
- Rollback canary to v2.13 for us-west-2 (revert to previous config) OR reduce canary weight to 0%
- Temporarily set `max_batch_size=32` and `batch_timeout_ms=20` on canary nodes via k8s patch to observe
- Add temporary rate-limit in front of affected routes (customer-impacting but quick)

maya: I already told support-bot to notify customer we’re investigating and will apply mitigation shortly.

ashley: I'll patch canary to lower batch size now:```sh
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/inference-runtime MAX_BATCH_SIZE=32 BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=20 --record
```patch applied, pods restarting.

ops-bot: Automations: started a synthetic load job against us-west-2 routes to validate.

liam: After the patch, early numbers look better on traces for repro requests (I triggered two repro runs). p95 dropped ~30% in those tests. Still watching p99.

devon: Dashboard note for follow-up: unify panels to use the same aggregation — prefer raw histogram + histogram_quantile at the same resolution as our rollup window. Add an annotation for 'rollup vs raw' in dashboard to prevent confusion. Also add a small doc blurb in runbooks about batch-size vs tail latency tradeoff.

sre-lead: Postmortem actions:
- Repro and validate v2.14 in staging with canary-level traffic and kernel matrix before prod canary
- Update deploy checklist to include batch-config and kernel/driver compatibility checks
- Ensure dashboards include explicit queries and a link to runbook explaining differences between histogram rollup and quantile_over_time

maya: Customer notified: "We applied a temporary fix and are monitoring; we'll follow up with root cause and timeline for a permanent fix."

support-bot: Customer ticket #2321 updated by maya: "Mitigation applied — reverting canary batch settings and monitoring. Please let us know if you see further slowness."

maya: Closing here for now — monitoring for 30m. If p99 remains elevated we'll escalate to runtime team for a full rollback and deeper trace analysis. Thanks all :raised_hands:
